acceptance_criteria.criterion: {plan_dir}/.orchestrator-run.json is created immediately after thread_id resolution and before graph execution, with result, error, and duration_s set to null.
After a successful run the file is updated with result = "SUCCESS" and a correct duration_s; both the metadata file and the tombstone file exist.
After a run using --interrupt-on (with no errors), the file is updated with result = "INTERRUPTED".
When --resume is called with a terminal thread_id, the _is_run_terminal path writes the metadata file with result = "ERROR" before exiting.
All file writes are atomic: the temp file is written then renamed via os.replace(); a partial write never leaves a corrupt metadata file.
is_resume is true in the metadata when --resume was used to launch the run.

summary: Added _write_run_metadata() helper to cli.py that atomically writes .orchestrator-run.json via temp file + os.replace().
Inserted run-start write (result=null) after thread_id resolution and run_start_ts capture, before graph execution.
Inserted run-end write (result=SUCCESS/INTERRUPTED/ERROR) after the lock-release finally block, before the tombstone.
Inserted error write (result=ERROR) in the _is_run_terminal early-exit path inside the if args.resume: block.
Added .orchestrator-run.json pattern to .gitignore.
Created orchestrator/tests/test_run_metadata.py with 25 passing tests covering all acceptance criteria.

comments.note: cli.py: The tombstone write (after the lock finally block) and the new metadata write share identical _fatal computation logic. A minor refactor to compute _fatal once and pass it to both would eliminate the duplication, but is out of scope for this WP.

cli.py: The _write_error_status() inner helper and _write_run_metadata() both write to plan_dir on the _is_run_terminal path. They're complementary (different purposes / file paths), but having two side-effect writes in one early-exit branch is worth a comment for future maintainers.

cli.py: The run-end INTERRUPTED detection uses a string-contains check on outside_errors ('Interrupted' in e). This is functional but fragile; a dedicated flag or enum would be more robust if more interrupt sources are added later.

comments.note: cli.py _write_run_metadata(): If write_text() succeeds but os.replace() fails (rare same-directory replace failure), the .tmp file would be orphaned — the OSError catch does not clean it up. Practically harmless (same-dir os.replace is almost always atomic), but a finally: tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True) after the replace would be belt-and-suspenders. Not a blocking issue.

No live --interrupt-on integration test was run (would require a real LangGraph graph execution). The logic is covered by the unit test of _write_run_metadata(result='INTERRUPTED') and by code inspection confirming the bool(interrupt_before) branch in cli.py lines 958-965.

comments.note: orchestrator/src/cli.py _write_run_metadata(): Added `finally: tmp_path.unlink(missing_ok=True)` (wrapped in inner try/except OSError) after the os.replace() call. Cleans up the orphaned .tmp file if write_text() succeeds but os.replace() fails — a rare but possible same-directory replace failure. Non-behavioral in the success path (os.replace consumed the file). Preserves the 'never raises' contract via the inner try/except. All 25 existing tests pass unchanged.

orchestrator/src/cli.py: _meta_fatal computation at the metadata write block (lines ~960-967) and the _fatal computation at the tombstone block are near-identical. A minor refactor to compute this once before both blocks would reduce duplication. Out of scope for WP-001.

orchestrator/src/cli.py: INTERRUPTED detection uses `any('Interrupted' in e for e in outside_errors)`. A dedicated enum or flag would be more robust if more interrupt sources are added. Out of scope, but worth noting for future maintainers.

[documentation-forward] The .orchestrator-run.json file format (all fields: thread_id, plan_path, slug, started_at, is_resume, dry_run, log_filename, pid, result, error, duration_s) is not documented in the orchestrator README or manifest. The Documentation agent should add a schema table and lifecycle description (null while in progress → SUCCESS/INTERRUPTED/ERROR) to orchestrator/README.md or the relevant manifest doc.
